body.x: Most hygiene care products, from razor sanitizers to pacifier cleaners, are stationary household units. Once a user leaves home, blades, pacifiers and bottle accessories go without care until they return.
Shrinking the device is not the hard part. The harder question is whether UV-C light can still reach a target surface evenly inside a body that weighs 55 g.

better U, a Korean consumer appliance brand led by CEO Moyoung Kim, builds its products around that problem. At KES 2026, the company is exhibiting three of them and running live demonstrations throughout the show: Model PURE, a portable razor sanitizer; NeoPure, a portable care device for infant pacifiers; and Click, a digital golf stroke counter.

Model PURE places the razor head inside the unit, where UV-C LEDs sanitize the blade surface. It runs on USB-C charging and comes in three colors. NeoPure combines ultrasonic cleaning, UV-C sanitizing and storage in one unit with three operating modes, wired and wireless charging, an IPX6-rated water-resistant body and a medical-grade SUS304 stainless steel chamber. Click records a stroke with one button press on a white OLED display, uses a CR2032 battery and needs no smartphone app. The company's technology rests on three elements: UV-C LED optical design for confined spaces, a structure that runs ultrasonic cleaning and UV-C sanitizing in sequence in a single chamber, and a compact power design that pairs wired and wireless charging with low-power control.

better U keeps product planning and design in-house. Engineers with 25 years of R&D experience in the home appliance industry set the concept, specifications and industrial design, then bring in development partners for mechanical, electronic and optical work. The company holds five registered product patents in Korea. Germ-reduction performance of Model PURE and NeoPure has been tested at accredited testing institutions, and the company says it limits its marketing claims to what those test reports support. The products carry Korea Certification (KC), FCC, CE and RoHS marks.

Domestically, better U sells through its own online store and Naver Smart Store. Overseas, it is listed on Amazon US, Amazon Japan, Qoo10 Japan and Alibaba.com, and has registered its products on KOTRA's Buy Korea platform. It plans to target the United States with NeoPure, Japan with Model PURE and Southeast Asia with Click, and is seeking distributors of baby products and lifestyle appliances as well as online retailers experienced with Amazon and Qoo10. It is also open to ODM supply in markets where brand distribution is difficult.

The company is developing a portable personal hygiene product for adults that applies its ultrasonic cleaning and UV-C sanitizing technology, with a launch planned for the first half of next year. It also aims to move from overseas OEM and ODM production to Made-in-Korea production within three years. better U cites the cost of overseas certification, particularly the additional U.S. procedures for UV-C hygiene products, and the lack of channels to meet overseas buyers as its main obstacles.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
